text:
Stephen Halliday is getting his first real run in Ottawa's lineup. He's 24, a fourth-round pick in 2022, and playing 11 and a half minutes a night, up from eight and a half last season, with four of his six points on the power play.

His own chances are up too, to 1.23 expected goals per 60 from 0.75, which is the sign that matters most for a player trying to stick. His three goals came on 4.3 expected (the quality of his chances), and Ottawa has scored 6.3 fewer goals than expected with him on the ice, so his points are light.

The role is still fragile. He played under six minutes against the Rangers and under nine against San Jose, then 13.6 on Saturday. With William Eklund, Andre Burakovsky and Warren Foegele all out, the minutes are there for him to take; Ridly Greig's return tonight may take some back. He had 51 points in 71 AHL games two seasons ago. Our projection sees about 15 goals, a real season for a fourth-rounder.
